data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["ML ensemble base learners are typically not interchangeable after training; panel members trained on the same checklist may be more interchangeable","Leave-one-out in ML tests model stability; here it tests whether reliability comes from the procedure or from individual variation","ML ensembles aggregate predictions; non-expert panels may aggregate judgments through discussion or voting, introducing social dynamics absent in ML"],"overturn_conditions":["Panel members are not interchangeable despite identical training, invalidating the leave-one-out logic","The panel is too small for leave-one-out to produce meaningful variation","Social dynamics during panel judgment mean that leaving out one member changes the group's judgment process, not just its composition"],"shared_structure":["Leave-one-out analysis in ML ensembles tests whether ensemble performance depends on specific base learners","Panel members are analogous to base learners; the checklist is the shared feature set"],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_005"],"transfer_claims":["Leave-one-out analysis distinguishes procedure-driven reliability from member-driven reliability within a single evaluation","If reliability is checklist-driven, removing any member should not change accuracy","If reliability depends on individual members' idiosyncratic judgments, removing those members degrades accuracy, revealing compliance coincidence"]},"claim":"The panel will outperform the expert for objectively verifiable outcomes because the checklist operationalizes a decision boundary that is closer to the true generative boundary than the expert's intuition, provided the checklist was validated against the objective outcome measure. The single-evaluation discriminator is a leave-one-out analysis: for each item, recompute the panel's judgment using all members except the one who judged that item, and compare to the full panel's accuracy. If the panel's accuracy is unchanged by leaving out any individual member, the reliability gain is from the checklist (genuine); if accuracy degrades when leaving out specific members, the gain depends on individual judgment (compliance coincidence).","counterconditions":[{"case":"The checklist was not validated against the objective outcome measure and merely encodes expert heuristics","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"Panel members' judgments are not interchangeable despite identical checklist training, due to differences in feature extraction or attention","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The leave-one-out analysis has insufficient power because the panel is too small or the evaluation set is too limited","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"If the checklist is validated against the objective outcome, it encodes the correct decision boundary in articulable form. Panel members serve as interchangeable implementers of this boundary, so leaving any one out should not change the outcome. If the panel's reliability depends on specific members' judgments (not just checklist compliance), then leaving those members out will degrade accuracy, revealing that the panel's success is not from checklist compliance but from individual variation that happens to track the answer. The leave-one-out analysis is computable within a single evaluation and directly tests whether reliability is checklist-driven or member-driven.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
